A bag contains 150 jelly beans. Some of them are red and the rest are blue. The ratio of red to blue jelly beans is $2:3$.

What is the new ratio of red to blue jelly beans?

solutions.latex:
The ratio $2:3$ has $2+3=5$ parts, so each part is $150\div 5 = 30$ jelly beans.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{red} &= 2\times 30 = 60\\ \text{blue} &= 3\times 30 = 90 \end{aligned}$$
After Sophie eats 10 of each colour:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{red} &= 50\\ \text{blue} &= 80 \end{aligned}$$
The new ratio is

Lily wanted to estimate the number of fish in a lake.

She randomly captured 30 fish, then tagged and released them.

One week later she randomly captured 40 fish from the same lake. She found that 12 of these 40 fish were tagged.

What is the best estimate for the total number of fish in the lake?

solutions.latex:
Using the capture-recapture method, the proportion of tagged fish in the second sample estimates the proportion in the whole lake.

Let $N$ be the number of fish in the lake.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{12}{40}&=\dfrac{30}{N}\\ N&=\dfrac{30\times 40}{12}\\ &=100 \end{aligned}$$
So the best estimate is 100, option D.

parts.latex: What is 20 minutes to one-third of a day, expressed as a ratio in simplest form?

One-third of a day is:
$$\dfrac{1}{3}\times 24=8\text{ hours}=8\times 60=480\text{ minutes}$$
The ratio is then:
$$\begin{aligned} 20:480&=1:24 \end{aligned}$$
(dividing both parts by 20).

So the answer is option B.

A full container has 4.8 L of a mixture of cordial and water in the ratio $1 : 3$.

After removing 1.2 L of the mixture, more water is added to refill the container.

What is the ratio of cordial to water in the final mixture?

solutions.latex:
After removing 1.2 L, $3.6$ L remains, still in the ratio $1:3$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Cordial} &= \dfrac{3.6}{4} = 0.9 \text{ L} \\ \text{Water} &= \dfrac{3.6\times 3}{4} = 2.7 \text{ L} \end{aligned}$$
Adding 1.2 L of water gives $2.7 + 1.2 = 3.9$ L of water.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{cordial} : \text{water} &= 0.9 : 3.9 \\ &= 3 : 13 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the ratio of cordial to water is } 3:13$$

4543.stem:
A marmalade recipe requires 5 oranges, 2 lemons, and 800 grams of sugar per batch.

Adele decides to make a larger batch while maintaining the recipe's proportions. She uses 15 more oranges than lemons.

parts.latex: Determine the number of oranges Adele will need for this larger batch.
Using this information, calculate the total amount of sugar required for Adele's batch of marmalade.

solutions.latex:
Let $O$ be the number of oranges and $L$ the number of lemons. The recipe ratio gives $\dfrac{O}{L} = \dfrac{5}{2}$, and $O = L + 15$.
$$\dfrac{L+15}{L} = \dfrac{5}{2}$$
$$\begin{aligned} 2L + 30 &= 5L \\ 3L &= 30 \\ L &= 10 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} O &= 10 + 15 \\ &= 25 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 25 \text{ oranges}$$

Sugar is in proportion to oranges.
$$\dfrac{800}{5} = 160 \text{ g of sugar per orange}$$
$$\begin{aligned} 25\times 160 &= 4000 \text{ g} \\ &= 4 \text{ kg} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 4 \text{ kg of sugar}$$

solutions.latex:
Apply the trapezoidal rule with one application, $A \approx \dfrac{h}{2}(d_f + d_l)$, with $h = 40$ m and the two end measurements $30$ m and $10$ m.
$$\begin{aligned} A &\approx \dfrac{40}{2}(30 + 10) \\ &= 800 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
The volume is the total area times the depth of $2$ m.
$$\begin{aligned} V &= (\text{semicircle} + \text{irregular region})\times \text{depth} \\ &= \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\times \pi\times 10^2 + 800\right)\times 2 \\ &= 1914.16\ldots \text{ m}^3 \\ &\approx 1900 \text{ m}^3 \end{aligned}$$
Since $1 \text{ m}^3 = 1 \text{ kL}$, the capacity is $1900$ kL to 2 significant figures.

solutions.latex:
The ratio $7:18$ has $25$ parts. Scale it to $1000$ kL.
$$7:18 = 280:720$$
After the refill the total is $1900$ kL. Fresh water is $280 + 100$ and chlorinated water is the rest.
$$\text{fresh} = 280 + 100 = 380 \text{ kL}$$
$$\text{chlorinated} = 1900 - 380 = 1520 \text{ kL}$$
$$380 : 1520 = 1 : 4$$
$$\therefore\ \text{New ratio} = 1:4$$

The rain forms a rectangular prism, with the roof as its base and the depth of rain as its height.

Convert the depth to metres: $35 \text{ mm} = 0.035 \text{ m}$.
$$\begin{aligned} V &= 20\times 12\times 0.035 \\ &= 8.4 \text{ m}^3 \end{aligned}$$

Since $1 \text{ m}^3 = 1000$ litres:
$$\begin{aligned} 8.4\times 1000 &= 8400 \text{ L} \end{aligned}$$

The extra water in the tank forms a cylinder of volume $8.4 \text{ m}^3$ and radius $1.6$ m.

Using $V=\pi r^2 h$:
$$\begin{aligned} 8.4 &= \pi\times 1.6^2\times h \\ h &= \dfrac{8.4}{\pi\times 1.6^2} \\ &\approx 1.0444 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
The ratio petrol : oil is $40:1$, so the oil is $\dfrac{1}{40}$ of the petrol.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{oil} &= \dfrac{5}{40} \\ &= 0.125 \text{ litres} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Joe should add } 0.125 \text{ litres (125 mL) of oil}$$

The leftover fuel is in the ratio $40:1$, so it has $41$ parts in total.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{petrol} &= \dfrac{40}{41}\times 4.1 = 4 \text{ L} \\ \text{oil} &= \dfrac{1}{41}\times 4.1 = 0.1 \text{ L} \end{aligned}$$
For the lawnmower the ratio must be $25:1$. The petrol stays at $4$ litres, so the oil needed is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{oil} &= \dfrac{4}{25} \\ &= 0.16 \text{ L} \end{aligned}$$
Oil to add:
$$\begin{aligned} 0.16-0.1 &= 0.06 \text{ L} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Joe should add } 0.06 \text{ litres (60 mL) of oil}$$
criteria: Finds the amount of petrol ($4$ L) and the oil required ($0.16$ L), or equivalent merit

In the region of a tropical forest, 96 rare birds were captured, tagged and released. Five months later, 72 birds were recaptured from the same region, and it was found that 18 of these birds had previously been tagged.

Use the 'capture-recapture' method to give an estimate of the number of rare birds in this region of the forest.

In the capture-recapture method, the tagged proportion in the sample equals the tagged proportion in the whole population $p$.

$$\therefore\ 0.06 \text{ L (60 mL) of oil should be added}$$

parts.latex: In the region of a tropical forest, 96 rare birds were captured, tagged and released. Five months later, 72 birds were recaptured from the same region and it was found that 18 of these birds had previously been tagged. Use the 'capture-recapture' method to give an estimate of the number of rare birds in this region of the forest.

solutions.latex:
The tagged fraction in the sample equals the tagged fraction in the population. Let $p$ be the population.
$$\dfrac{96}{p}=\dfrac{18}{72}$$
$$\begin{aligned} p&=\dfrac{96\times72}{18} \\ &=384 \end{aligned}$$
The number of rare birds is $384$.
criteria: Sets up the ratio, or equivalent merit

A tradesman is employed to pain the ceiling of Bedroom 1. He paints at a constant rate of $12\,\text{m}^2$ per hour and is paid at a rate of $\$62$ per hour to the nearest whole number of hours.

Measuring the floor plan, the bedroom is $4.3$ cm by $3.7$ cm.

\exfigure{711_q24_s1}

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Length}&=4.3\times125 \\ &=537.5\text{ cm} \\ &=5.375\text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
Two coats means twice the area.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area}&=2\times5.375\times4.625 \\ &=49.71875\text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
Time at $12\text{ m}^2$ per hour:
$$49.71875\div12\approx4.143\text{ hours}$$
Paid to the nearest whole number of hours, so he is paid for 5 hours.
$$\text{Cost}=62\times5=\$310$$
Since $\$310<\$350$, the owner has sufficient funds.

parts.latex:
For school sports, 35 students, out of a total of 90 students, choose to play football.

The rest choose to play cricket.

What is the ratio of cricket players to footballers?

solutions.latex:
The number of cricket players is the total minus the footballers.
$$90-35=55$$
The ratio of cricket players to footballers is
$$\begin{aligned} 55:35 &= 11:7 &&(\text{divide both by } 5) \end{aligned}$$
Hence the ratio is $11:7$, option D.

parts.latex:
A rectangular block of land, that measures 150 m by 80 m, has a footpath, of length 100 m, across it.

On the survey map, this block of land is represented by an area of 3 cm by 1.6 cm.

What is the length of the path, on the survey map, across the block of land?

solutions.latex:
Find the scale from the block: $150 \text{ m}$ is represented by $3 \text{ cm}$ (and $80 \text{ m}$ by $1.6 \text{ cm}$).
$$\begin{aligned} 3 \text{ cm} &= 150 \text{ m} \\ 1 \text{ cm} &= 50 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

The path is $100 \text{ m}$ long, so its length on the map is
$$\dfrac{100}{50} = 2 \text{ cm}$$

This is option B.

parts.latex:
A dam, shown below, is located on a rectangular block of land.

All measurements are in metres.

\exfigure{1264_q24_1}

Use the trapezoidal rule to calculate the approximate surface area of the dam.

solutions.latex:
The trapezoidal rule with width $h=30$ and three function values $0, 16, 0$ gives
$$\begin{aligned} A &\approx \dfrac{30}{2}\left[0+2\times 16+0\right] \\ &= 15\times 32 \\ &= 480 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
Alternatively, area of rectangle minus the area of 4 trapezia:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 60\times 40-\left[15(12+15)+15(15+25)+15(28+9)+15(9+15)\right] \\ &= 480 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Area}\approx 480 \text{ m}^2$$

A marine biologist used the capture-recapture technique to estimate the number of fish in a lake. He captured, tagged and released 28 fish. Later he caught 35 at random and found that 4 had been tagged. What is the estimate for the total fish in the lake?

solutions.latex:
The tagged fraction in the sample equals the tagged fraction in the lake.

$$\dfrac{28}{x} = \dfrac{4}{35}$$
$$\dfrac{x}{28} = \dfrac{35}{4}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &= \dfrac{35}{4} \times 28 \\ &= 245 \end{aligned}$$

The estimate is $245$ fish.

parts.latex: The ratio of cars to motorbikes in a car park is $8:3$ and the ratio of motorbikes to vans is $5:2$. If there are 160 cars, find the total number of vehicles in the car park.

solutions.latex:
Matching the motorbikes, with cars : motorbikes $= 8:3 = 40:15$ and motorbikes : vans $= 5:2 = 15:6$:

$$\text{cars} : \text{motorbikes} : \text{vans} = 40 : 15 : 6$$

Since $40$ parts $= 160$ cars, $1$ part $= 4$ cars.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= 160 + (15 \times 4) + (6 \times 4) \\ &= 244 \text{ vehicles} \end{aligned}$$
